strengths: MSAM addresses a meaningful practical problem with a simple modification: it reuses momentum for perturbations and requires one forward/backward pass. Table 1 reports relative speed of 0.99 versus 0.52 for SAM, supporting the computational advantage.

The reported improvements over baseline optimizers are substantial in several settings: WRN-16-4 on CIFAR100 improves from 76.90% to 79.11%, and ViT-S/32 on ImageNet improves from 67.0% to 69.1%. The matched-compute experiments provide useful additional evidence.

Extensive ablations investigate perturbation sign, normalization, learning rate, momentum, batch size, alternative directions, and compatibility with adaptive and BatchNorm-only perturbations. The observations about overshooting and decoupling perturbation magnitude from the learning rate are informative.

The core algorithm is clearly presented and situated relative to SAM, NAG, and extragradient methods. A code link, training configurations, and full hyperparameter scans aid reproducibility. Instability and the imperfect relationship between sharpness and generalization are openly discussed.
weaknesses: The generalization argument in Appendix A.1 is invalid as stated. Proposition 1 fails for negative Hessian trace: with H = diag(1, -3), a standard Gaussian perturbation, and radius 1, its left side is approximately -0.1804 while its right side is -1. Setting 1 does not exclude this case. Theorem 3 also invokes the SAM PAC-Bayes proof without establishing the required loss restrictions, population-risk relationship, Gaussian-tail control, or Taylor-remainder assumptions. Consequently, Section 4.1's claim that improved generalization follows theoretically is unsupported.

The main ImageNet comparison uses unequal warm-up policies. MSAM perturbations are disabled during warm-up, whereas SAM perturbations remain enabled despite the authors finding that disabling them improves SAM. Table A.2 reports 69.8% for SAM with this adjustment versus 69.1% for MSAM. The computational advantage remains credible, but the headline accuracy-parity comparison needs equally tuned schedules.

Model selection and uncertainty are insufficiently established. Appendix A.15 reports the best perturbation strengths alongside curves labeled test accuracy without describing an independent validation-selection procedure. Most ImageNet results are single runs; uncertainty measured for smaller baseline models does not establish uncertainty for other models or optimizers. The 0.07 BLEU advantage over SAM likewise lacks uncertainty estimates.

The broad accuracy-preservation and dominance claims exceed the results. MSAM trails SAM by 2.4 percentage points on ViT-S/16 at 300 epochs and by 2.0 points on ViT-B/16. Matched-compute evaluations cover WRN-16-4 and ViT-S/32, leaving recovery of these larger gaps untested. Table 1 also does not show uniform accuracy superiority over LookSAM.

The interpretation as full-training-set sharpness minimization remains unverified. Momentum averages gradients at changing parameter locations, and its approximation to the current full-data gradient is not quantified. Random-direction flatness does not establish worst-case sharpness reduction. Figure 3 discards the component orthogonal to the SAM/SGD plane, so alignment of the projection cannot establish similarity of the complete updates. These limitations weaken the mechanistic contribution beyond the useful empirical observations.
